findings.finding: Counter-thesis (pre-mortem, 2029): ServiceNow failed as an investment because AI agents (Microsoft Copilot/agents, Salesforce Agentforce, in-house builds on frontier models) moved the workflow layer above the system of record. Seat-based ITSM/CSM expansion slowed: organic growth fell into the low-to-mid teens while reported growth was held up by about 11.2B USD of 2025-2026 acquisitions (Armis, Moveworks, Veza). SBC stayed near 15% of revenue and acquisition amortization stayed high, so GAAP EPS never caught up with the non-GAAP story. Debt-funded deals (debt 1.5B to 7.5B, 2.1B commercial paper rolled about every 62 days, Altman Z'' 2.18 grey) cut the return on capital toward the bear's 15%. The multiple de-rated to about 20x GAAP. Early signs: (1) organic cRPO, which is not disclosed today (gap), or cRPO cc at or below 18% in Q4 2026 / Q1 2027 with Armis lapping in Q2 2027; (2) the 98% renewal rate falling, or net new ACV in core ITSM going flat while AI ACV grows (cannibalization rather than additive); (3) SBC/revenue not falling in FY2027; (4) more acquisitions, or CP refinanced into term debt; (5) federal channel-partner or DOJ news. Only some of this is in the bear (see the next findings), and the seat-compression mechanism is labelled a hypothesis with no evidence id.
findings.where: position/core.json scenario_events.bear (the seat-compression event has no evidence_ids); companies/NOW/out/table_he.md risk row
findings.fix: Keep the AI seat-compression event explicitly marked as a hypothesis, or attach evidence (named-competitor agent pricing, NOW seat/renewal data). Add a numeric falsifier for the counter-thesis, e.g. Q2 2027 cRPO cc (first quarter fully lapping Armis) below 17% by 2027-08-15 confirms the bear, and a renewal-rate threshold below 97% by FY2027.

findings.finding: The bear barely changes the business; the multiple does most of the work. Bear revenue in FY2027 is 18.72B vs base 19.29B (-3%), and bear EPS in year 1 is 2.71 vs base 2.93 (-8%). Yet the year-1 price is 59.9 vs 164 (-63%), driven by 22x vs 56x. The bear GAAP operating margin still rises from 12.3% (FY2027) to 20% by FY2030, above the company's best reported GAAP margin (13.7% FY2025; Q3 2026 was 9.5%). The guardrail is close to 'one EPS path x three multiples' for years 0-2. The bear's named mechanisms are not sized from their shares: a federal channel partner at 12% of revenue and 20% of receivables, plus an unresolved DOJ investigation with debarment risk, gives only a 3.5pp lower growth anchor (15.5% vs 19%) and no margin hit.
findings.where: position/core.json drivers.bear (growth_anchor 0.155, mature_margin 0.2); casefile.json company_path.scenarios.bear.rows; position/coherence.md bear
findings.fix: Size the bear mechanisms from evidence: a federal-channel disruption on its 12% share (e.g. 2027 growth cut by part of that share), organic growth ex-Armis/Moveworks, and a bear mature margin after SBC no higher than the best reported GAAP margin unless an evidenced SBC/amortization fade supports it. Rerun ticker-value so the bear EPS path diverges from the base.

findings.finding: SBC fade is an unevidenced lever that lifts every scenario. Reported SBC is 14.7% of revenue (FY2025) and about 15.5% in Q3 2026, up about 29% y/y; Q3 buybacks were zero and Q4 diluted shares are guided at 1.05B. Over the horizon the model charges SBC at about 10.9% of revenue (bear 10.95%, base 10.85%, bull 10.79%) and holds weighted shares flat at 1,038M in every year of every scenario. The table lists SBC under 'assumptions without company data'. The risk register's dil.sbc (severity high) has pricing_status not_priced and is not in the bear. With SBC held near 15%, the mature margins after SBC (20/26/30%) fall by about 4pp and the yearly prices fall with them.
findings.where: casefile.json rv.mechanical.redteam.derived_inputs.sbc_treatment; rk.register dil.sbc; company_path rows weighted_shares; table_he.md row 'הנחות בלי נתון של החברה'
findings.fix: Hold SBC at the reported ~15% in the bear (and justify any base fade with company evidence: management SBC targets, the trend), model share count from the Q4 guide of 1.05B plus net dilution when buybacks pause, and put dil.sbc into the bear. Otherwise state next to the result that the margins assume SBC falls by about a third with no company data.

findings.finding: The base multiple path rests on a 30% return on capital, above the company's own measured record. The analyst's own base reason computes incremental after-tax operating income / added capital for 2022-2025 at about 20%. Forensic ROIC is 14.0% last year and 9.3% on average (prefetch/forensic.json). The analyst argues 20% is biased down and that acquisitions dilute it, then picks 30% anyway. The result is base multiples of 71.7x (year 0) and 56.1x (year 1) on GAAP EPS, against 50.6x implied by today's price on the same FY2027 EPS. The label justified_high / tier own_history overstates the evidence: the base yearly prices (164 to 238, '+125% in 5 years') depend on it.
findings.where: position/path.json scenarios.base.roic (0.3) and reason_he; casefile.json company_path.scenarios.base.multiple_path
findings.fix: Set the base roic to the evidenced ~20% (or a blend that explicitly charges the 11.2B of acquisitions at their own lower return), or label the base multiple 'unproven' and state it next to the table. Rerun ticker-value.

findings.finding: The table's 5-year potential row understates the downside the owner's buy test reads. It shows 'דובי -15%' (year-5 bear 89.8). But the bear path passes 52.1 at year 0 and 59.9 at year 1 (-43%). The engine's DCF bear value today is 49.6 (rv derived scenario_values), and at the required return it is 32.8 (dc.verdict.margin_of_safety loss_to_bear 69%). The +125% base / +312% bull rows also sit next to a base IRR of 11.0% and bull IRR of 13.4%. The yearly EPS x multiple prices and the DCF disagree by a wide margin, and a reader takes the larger numbers.
findings.where: companies/NOW/out/table_he.md row 'פוטנציאל בעוד 5 שנים'; casefile.json dc.expected_return, dc.verdict.margin_of_safety
findings.fix: Next to the result, state the bear today (~50, about -53%) and the max drawdown on the bear path, and that the base/bull IRRs (11.0% / 13.4%) are the cash-flow returns. If the base roic is corrected (finding above), regenerate the table.

findings.finding: The falsifiers do not separate the scenarios. Base fx_base_subrev_fy26 (subscription revenue FY2026 below 15.7B) is effectively already decided: two months remain, the guide stands, and the company beat the guided midpoint in all 7 quarters read. Bull fx_bull_ai_acv (AI ACV below 1.7B at end FY2026) tests the management target that is also a base event, so hitting it does not confirm the bull over the base. Nothing tests organic growth, the 98% renewal rate, SBC/revenue or the return on the 11.2B of acquisitions, which are the levers the scenarios actually differ on.
findings.fix: Replace them with discriminating numeric tests, e.g. bull: FY2027 subscription revenue growth cc at or above 21% by 2028-02-15, or AI ACV above 2.5B by end FY2027; base: renewal rate below 97% or SBC/revenue above 15% in FY2027 refutes; bear: GAAP operating margin FY2027 at or above 16% refutes.

findings.finding: Base growth anchor 19% equals cRPO cc growth, which includes Armis (closed 2026-04-20) and Moveworks contributions. The organic rate is undisclosed (an evidence-pack gap). The base calls this the organic engine, so 2027 base growth includes about four months of inorganic Armis contribution.
findings.where: position/core.json drivers.base growth_anchor; evidence_pack dc note on cRPO
findings.fix: State next to the base that 19% is reported (incl. acquisitions), or haircut it for the Armis lap from Q2 2027.

findings.finding: Data QA records the split as 'x25 between 2025-09-30 and 2025-12-31'. The evidence pack and identity say 5-for-1. Own-history P/E (75.8-243, median 91.7) looks consistent with a x5 restatement, but the flag should be reconciled so the own_history tier is not built on mis-restated EPS.
findings.fix: Confirm the per-share history uses a 5x restatement and clear or correct the x25 corporate-action reading.

findings.finding: Funding and financing in the bear: the risk register's exe.stress_funding_gap (high, not priced) and the 2.1B commercial paper rolled about every 62 days at 4.05% are not in the bear. Bear cash flows stay strongly positive, so this is a refinancing-cost and flexibility risk rather than a solvency risk. The Altman grey zone is carried only as text.
findings.fix: Add one bear line on CP refinancing at a higher rate and no buybacks, or state that the stress funding gap is not priced.

findings.finding: expectation_gap was not rerun separately in this review (budget). The table's 'what the price assumes' row (about 7% real growth for 10 years, 27% base rate for this size) and redteam_audit (verdict passed: cash, debt and shares reconcile) were read from the casefile. The low implied requirement is consistent with a large de-rating already in the price (105.34 USD post-split).
findings.fix: None required. Optional: run expectation_gap with company drivers in the repair pass if the base roic or SBC is changed.
